title: CmdPal: Disposing a dock leaves its bands alive (EXT26.C1-C2)

judgment.rationale: An isolated test found zero cleanup across three groups; queued publication/initialization is source-based and was not tested with a real dispatcher or monitor transition. Both parts need targeted validation.
judgment.recommended_action: Use the targeted maintainer reproduction to validate the proposed mechanism before design approval; no upstream action has been taken.
evidence: The report reproduces zero cleanup across StartItems, CenterItems and EndItems after owner disposal.
It separately identifies queued setup without an owner-disposal check; no real dispatcher or monitor transition was tested.
The cited DockViewModel and DockWindowManager source areas are present.

fix_assessment.rationale: No matching fix was identified by focused issue-number search; keep the mechanism as a hypothesis pending reproduction.

plan: Close setup admission at owner disposal and recheck lifetime in queued callbacks before publishing or initializing.
Drain/clean current bands from all groups without remote cleanup on UI thread.
Clean candidates rejected after disposal and keep repeated disposal harmless.
Add dispatcher-controlled queued-work and dock-recreation tests.
verification: Dispose a dock with bands in all three groups and verify each is cleaned.
Pause queued publication/initialization, dispose, release work, and verify no repopulation or subscriptions.
Recreate the dock and verify normal initialization.
proposed_fixes.title: Correct the reported Command Palette lifecycle failure
proposed_fixes.root_cause: DockViewModel.Dispose marks the owner disposed but does not clean its three band groups; queued SetupBands work may proceed after disposal and repopulate collections or subscriptions.

confidence.rationale: Three-group cleanup failure is isolated-test evidence; dispatcher ordering and late candidate cleanup need verification.
